The FBI's director, Chris Rea, is planning to retire around the end of the year.
He's the third person to leave the number two job at the bureau during the Trump administration,
as NPR's Ryan Lucas reports.
Chris Rea has been serving as deputy director for less than a year.
He was put in the job after right-wing podcast host Dan Bongino left the post early this
year.
He was interviewed as co-deputy director alongside former Missouri Attorney General Andrew Bailey
before Bailey stepped down this fall.
Unlike Bongino and Bailey, Rea is a career FBI agent who rose up through the ranks.
He was viewed by many inside the bureau as a steadying presence amid all the turmoil
under FBI Director Cash Patel.
Neither the FBI nor Patel has commented on Rea's planned departure.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
The Iraqi government has announced a major move to take back control of important oil
fields operated by the country's Kurdish regional government.
As NPR's Jane Araff reports, it widens the rift between Baghdad and Iraq's Kurdistan
region.
The Iraqi government says the move is part of a crackdown across the country on oil smuggling.
Baghdad and the semi-autonomous Kurdistan region have long disagreed over the share
of oil revenue going to the Kurds.
Now Prime Minister Ali Azadi says the federal ministry will manage some of the biggest fields
under Kurdish control.
He has also directed that Kurdish checkpoints between federal government controlled Iraq
and the Kurdish provinces be dismantled.
Kurdish leaders have rejected the moves and rejected allegations of oil smuggling.
Jane Araff, NPR News, Amman.
Federal aviation and transportation officials are investigating the crash of a small plane
off the coast of Mississippi yesterday that left all six people on board, including two
children, dead.
You're listening to NPR News.
The music streaming service TIDAL is banning music made entirely using generative AI.
NPR's Chloe Bellman reports it makes TIDAL among the few major platforms to take this
step.
TIDAL announced on social media that its ban on tracks created solely with AI will take
effect on December 9th, but tracks made with help from AI will still be permitted.
The company says over the past three months more than 40 percent of all tracks on its
platforms are totally AI-generated and that less than five percent of them receive even
a single stream.
TIDAL expects to remove roughly 27 million AI tracks by 2027.
Dan Macter is a managing director for TIDAL competitor Cobuz.
He says his company is also trying to figure out how to solve the AI slop problem, but
he says detecting and banning offending tracks is unlikely to work.
Because the AI will figure out how to create content that's not detectable.
Meanwhile, the largest music streamers, Apple and Spotify, still allow songs made completely
with AI to appear on their platforms.
Chloe Bellman, NPR News.
A strong storm with heavy rain, strong gusty winds and coastal flooding is forecast to
slam parts of the east coast today through tomorrow, threatening Thanksgiving Day holiday
plans from the Carolinas through New England.
The National Weather Service says the storm will intensify as it heads north, with showers
and severe thunderstorms possible along with those strong winds.
Heavy rain could lead to flash flooding and officials say travel disruptions and power

I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.
